verses.zh: 耶和华对约书亚说：「不要惧怕，也不要惊惶。你起来，率领一切兵丁上艾城去，我已经把艾城的王和他的民、他的城，并他的地，都交在你手里。
verses.en: The Lord told Joshua, “Don’t be afraid and don’t panic![NOTE:1] Take the whole army with you and march against Ai![NOTE:2] See, I am handing over to you[NOTE:3] the king of Ai, along with his people, city, and land.
notes: Or perhaps “and don’t get discouraged!”
Heb “Take with you all the people of war and arise, go up against Ai!”
Heb “I have given into our hand.” The verbal form, a perfect, is probably best understood as a perfect of certitude, indicating the certainty of the action.

verses.zh: 你怎样待耶利哥和耶利哥的王，也当照样待艾城和艾城的王。只是城内所夺的财物和牲畜，你们可以取为自己的掠物。你要在城后设下伏兵。」
verses.en: Do to Ai and its king what you did to Jericho[NOTE:1] and its king, except you may plunder its goods and cattle. Set an ambush behind the city.”
notes: For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

verses.zh: 于是，约书亚和一切兵丁都起来，要上艾城去。约书亚选了三万大能的勇士，夜间打发他们前往，
verses.en: Joshua and the whole army marched against Ai.[NOTE:1] Joshua selected 30,000 brave warriors and sent them out at night.
notes: “And Joshua and all the people of war arose to go up [against] Ai.”

verses.zh: 吩咐他们说：「你们要在城后埋伏，不可离城太远，都要各自准备。
verses.en: He ordered them, “Look, set an ambush behind the city. Don’t go very far from the city; all of you be ready!

verses.zh: 我与我所带领的众民要向城前往。城里的人像初次出来攻击我们的时候，我们就在他们面前逃跑，
verses.en: I and all the troops[NOTE:1] who are with me will approach the city. When they come out to fight us like before, we will retreat from them.
notes: Heb “the people.”

verses.zh: 他们必出来追赶我们，直到我们引诱他们离开城；因为他们必说：『这些人像初次在我们面前逃跑。』所以我们要在他们面前逃跑，
verses.en: They will attack[NOTE:1] us until we have lured them from the city, for they will say, ‘They are retreating from us like before.’ We will retreat from them.
notes: Heb “come out after.”

verses.zh: 你们就从埋伏的地方起来，夺取那城，因为耶和华―你们的　神必把城交在你们手里。
verses.en: Then you rise up from your hiding place[NOTE:1] and seize[NOTE:2] the city. The Lord your God will hand it over to you.
notes: Heb “from the ambush.”
Heb “take possession of.”

verses.zh: 你们夺了城以后，就放火烧城，要照耶和华的话行。这是我吩咐你们的。」
verses.en: When you capture the city, set it[NOTE:1] on fire in keeping with the Lord’s message. See, I have given you orders.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the city.”
Heb “I have commanded you.”

verses.zh: 约书亚打发他们前往，他们就上埋伏的地方去，住在伯特利和艾城的中间，就是在艾城的西边。这夜约书亚却在民中住宿。
verses.en: Joshua sent them away and they went to their hiding place[NOTE:1] west of Ai, between Bethel[NOTE:2] and Ai.[NOTE:3] Joshua spent that night with the army.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “the place of ambush.”
For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
Heb “and they stayed between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai.”
Heb “in the midst of the people.”

verses.zh: 约书亚清早起来，点齐百姓，他和以色列的长老在百姓前面上艾城去。
verses.en: Bright and early the next morning Joshua gathered[NOTE:1] the army,[NOTE:2] and he and the leaders[NOTE:3] of Israel marched[NOTE:4] at the head of it[NOTE:5] to Ai.
notes: Or “summoned, mustered.”
Heb “the people.”
Or “elders.”
Heb “went up.”

Heb “them” (referring to “the people” in the previous clause, which requires a plural pronoun). Since the translation used “army” in the previous clause, a singular pronoun (“it”) is required in English.

verses.zh: 众民，就是他所带领的兵丁，都上去，向前直往，来到城前，在艾城北边安营。在约书亚和艾城中间有一山谷。
verses.en: All the troops that were with him marched up and drew near the city.[NOTE:1] They camped north of Ai on the other side of the valley.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “All the people of war who were with him went up and approached and came opposite the city.”
Heb “and the valley [was] between them and Ai.”

verses.zh: 他挑了约有五千人，使他们埋伏在伯特利和艾城的中间，就是在艾城的西边，
verses.en: He took 5,000 men and set an ambush west of the city between Bethel[NOTE:1] and Ai.
notes: For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

verses.zh: 于是安置了百姓，就是城北的全军和城西的伏兵。这夜约书亚进入山谷之中。
verses.en: The army was in position—the main army north of the city and the rear guard west of the city. That night Joshua went into[NOTE:1] the middle of the valley.
notes: Some Hebrew mss read, “spent the night in.”

verses.zh: 艾城的王看见这景况，就和全城的人，清早急忙起来，按所定的时候，出到亚拉巴前，要与以色列人交战；王却不知道在城后有伏兵。
verses.en: When the king of Ai and all his people saw Israel, they rushed to get up early. Then the king and the men of the city went out to meet Israel in battle, at the meeting place near the rift valley.[NOTE:1] But he did not realize an ambush was waiting for him behind the city.[NOTE:2]
notes: This probably refers to the hill country at the edge of the rift valley between Ai and Jericho. This part of the battle was probably engaged where Israel would have come up to the hill country out of the rift valley from Jericho, an ascent of about 4000 feet (with ups and downs) over ten miles.
Heb “did not know that an ambush for him was behind the city.”

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列众人在他们面前装败，往那通旷野的路逃跑。
verses.en: Joshua and all Israel pretended to be defeated by them, and they retreated along the way to the wilderness.

verses.zh: 城内的众民都被招聚，追赶他们；艾城人追赶的时候，就被引诱离开城。
verses.en: All the reinforcements[NOTE:1] in Ai[NOTE:2] were ordered[NOTE:3] to chase them; they chased Joshua and were lured away from the city.
notes: Heb “All the people.”
Some textual witnesses read “the city.”
Or “were summoned”; or “were mustered.”

verses.zh: 艾城和伯特利城没有一人不出来追赶以色列人的，撇了敞开的城门，去追赶以色列人。
verses.en: No men were left in Ai or Bethel;[NOTE:1] they all went out after Israel.[NOTE:2] They left the city wide open and chased Israel.
notes: The LXX omits the words “or Bethel.”map For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
Heb “who did not go out after Israel.”

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐约书亚说：「你向艾城伸出手里的短枪，因为我要将城交在你手里。」约书亚就向城伸出手里的短枪。
verses.en: The Lord told Joshua, “Hold out toward Ai the curved sword[NOTE:1] in your hand, for I am handing the city[NOTE:2] over to you.” So Joshua held out toward Ai the curved sword in his hand.
notes: Traditionally “spear,” but see HALOT 472 s.v. כִּידוֹן, which argues based upon evidence from the Dead Sea Scrolls that this term refers to a curved sword of some type; note the definition “scimitar” given there.
Heb “it”; the referent (the city of Ai) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他一伸手，伏兵就从埋伏的地方急忙起来，夺了城，跑进城去，放火焚烧。
verses.en: When he held out his hand, the men waiting in ambush rose up quickly from their place and attacked.[NOTE:1] They entered the city, captured it, and immediately set it on fire.
notes: Heb “and ran.”

verses.zh: 艾城的人回头一看，不料，城中烟气冲天，他们就无力向左向右逃跑。那往旷野逃跑的百姓便转身攻击追赶他们的人。
verses.en: When the men of Ai turned around, they saw[NOTE:1] the smoke from the city ascending into the sky and were so shocked they were unable to flee in any direction.[NOTE:2] In the meantime the men who were retreating to the wilderness turned against their pursuers.
notes: Heb “and they saw, and look.” The Hebrew term הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) draws attention to the scene and invites the audience to view the events from the perspective of the men of Ai.
Heb “and there was not in them hands to flee here or there.” The Hebrew term יָדַיִם (yadayim, “hands”) is idiomatic for “strength.”

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列众人见伏兵已经夺了城，城中烟气飞腾，就转身回去，击杀艾城的人。
verses.en: When Joshua and all Israel saw that the men in ambush had captured the city and that the city was going up in smoke,[NOTE:1] they turned around and struck down the men of Ai.
notes: Heb “and that the smoke of the city ascended.”

verses.zh: 伏兵也出城迎击艾城人，艾城人就困在以色列人中间，前后都是以色列人。于是以色列人击杀他们，没有留下一个，也没有一个逃脱的，
verses.en: At the same time the men who had taken the city came out to fight, and the men of Ai were trapped in the middle.[NOTE:1] The Israelites struck them down, leaving no survivors or refugees.
notes: Heb “and these went out from the city to meet them and they were for Israel in the middle, some on this side, and others on the other side.”

verses.zh: 生擒了艾城的王，将他解到约书亚那里。
verses.en: But they captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

verses.zh: 以色列人在田间和旷野杀尽所追赶一切艾城的居民。艾城人倒在刀下，直到灭尽；以色列众人就回到艾城，用刀杀了城中的人。
verses.en: When Israel had finished killing all the men[NOTE:1] of Ai who had chased them toward the wilderness[NOTE:2] (they all fell by the sword),[NOTE:3] all Israel returned to Ai and put the sword to it.
notes: Heb “residents.”
Heb “in the field, in the wilderness in which they chased them.”
Heb “and all of them fell by the edge of the sword until they were destroyed.” The LXX omits the words, “and all of them fell by the edge of the sword.” They may represent a later scribal addition.

verses.zh: 当日杀毙的人，连男带女共有一万二千，就是艾城所有的人。
verses.en: So 12,000 men and women died[NOTE:1] that day, including all the men of Ai.
notes: Heb “fell.”

verses.zh: 约书亚没有收回手里所伸出来的短枪，直到把艾城的一切居民尽行杀灭。
verses.en: Joshua kept holding out his curved sword until Israel had annihilated all who lived in Ai.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Joshua did not draw back his hand which held out the curved sword until he had annihilated all the residents of Ai.”

verses.zh: 惟独城中的牲畜和财物，以色列人都取为自己的掠物，是照耶和华所吩咐约书亚的话。
verses.en: But Israel did plunder the cattle and the goods of the city, in keeping with the Lord’s orders[NOTE:1] to Joshua.
notes: Heb “message, word.”

verses.zh: 约书亚将艾城焚烧，使城永为高堆、荒场，直到今日；
verses.en: Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanently uninhabited mound (it remains that way to this very day).[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and made it a permanent mound, a desolation, to this day.”

verses.zh: 又将艾城王挂在树上，直到晚上。日落的时候，约书亚吩咐人把尸首从树上取下来，丢在城门口，在尸首上堆成一大堆石头，直存到今日。
verses.en: He hung the king of Ai on a tree, leaving him exposed until evening.[NOTE:1] At sunset Joshua ordered that his corpse be taken down from the tree.[NOTE:2] They threw it down at the entrance of the city gate and erected over it a large pile of stones (it remains to this very day).[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “on a tree until evening.” The words “leaving him exposed” are supplied in the translation for clarity.
For the legal background of this action, see Deut 21:22-23.
Heb “to this day.”

verses.zh: 那时，约书亚在以巴路山上为耶和华―以色列的　神筑一座坛，
verses.en: Then Joshua built an altar for the Lord God of Israel on Mount Ebal,

verses.zh: 是用没有动过铁器的整石头筑的，照着耶和华仆人摩西所吩咐以色列人的话，正如摩西律法书上所写的。众人在这坛上给耶和华奉献燔祭和平安祭。
verses.en: just as Moses the Lord’s servant had commanded the Israelites. As described in the law scroll of Moses, it was made with uncut stones untouched by an iron tool.[NOTE:1] On it they offered burnt sacrifices to the Lord and sacrificed tokens of peace.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “as it is written in the scroll of the law of Moses, an altar of whole stones on which no one had wielded iron.” The expression “whole stones” refers to stones in their natural condition, i.e., not carved or shaped artificially with tools (“wielded iron”).
Or “peace offerings.”

verses.zh: 约书亚在那里，当着以色列人面前，将摩西所写的律法抄写在石头上。
verses.en: There, in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua inscribed on the stones a duplicate of the law written by Moses.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he wrote there on the stones a duplicate of the law of Moses which he wrote before the sons of Israel.”

verses.zh: 以色列众人，无论是本地人、是寄居的，和长老、官长，并审判官，都站在约柜两旁，在抬耶和华约柜的祭司利未人面前，一半对着基利心山，一半对着以巴路山，为以色列民祝福，正如耶和华仆人摩西先前所吩咐的。
verses.en: All the people,[NOTE:1] rulers,[NOTE:2] leaders, and judges were standing on either side of the ark, in front of the Levitical priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord. Both resident foreigners and native Israelites were there.[NOTE:3] Half the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and the other half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the Lord’s servant had previously instructed them to do for the formal blessing ceremony.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “All Israel.”
Or “elders.”
Heb “like the resident foreigner, like the citizen.” The language is idiomatic, meaning that both groups were treated the same, at least in this instance.
Heb “as Moses, the Lord’s servant, commanded to bless the people, Israel, formerly.”sn Moses’ earlier instructions are found in Deut 11:29.

verses.zh: 随后，约书亚将律法上祝福、咒诅的话，照着律法书上一切所写的，都宣读了一遍。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Joshua read aloud all the words of the law, including the blessings and the curses, just as they are written in the law scroll.
notes: Or “afterward.”

verses.zh: 摩西所吩咐的一切话，约书亚在以色列全会众和妇女、孩子，并他们中间寄居的外人面前，没有一句不宣读的。
verses.en: Joshua read aloud every commandment Moses had given[NOTE:1] before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, children, and resident foreigners who lived among them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “There was not a word from all which Moses commanded that Joshua did not read aloud.”
Heb “walked in their midst.”
